tutorial.title: Tutorial
tutorial.subtitle: Follow these steps to master OpenArma's core features and complete your first multi-agent collaboration.
tutorial.resetDesc: Clear all completed step markers and start the tutorial over.
tutorial.step1Desc: Add a large language model provider — the foundation for AI conversations.
tutorial.step1_1: Go to "LLM Providers" in the sidebar
tutorial.step1_2: Click "Add Provider" and select a preset (e.g., DeepSeek, OpenAI)
tutorial.step1_3: The API URL is auto-filled; just enter your API Key
tutorial.step1_4: Once saved, the provider is available for agents to use
tutorial.step1Tip1: DeepSeek is recommended for fast access and good value in China
tutorial.step1Tip2: You can add multiple providers and choose per-agent later
tutorial.step2Desc: Agents are the core of AI conversations, each with a unique role and capabilities.
tutorial.step2_2: Click "Create Agent" and fill in the name and description
tutorial.step2_3: Write a System Prompt to define the agent's role and behavior
tutorial.step2_4: Select an LLM provider and model
tutorial.step2_5: Optional: Enable built-in tools (web search, knowledge retrieval)
tutorial.step2Tip1: Create 2-3 agents with different roles (e.g., "Tech Analyst", "Market Researcher", "Product Manager") to experience multi-agent collaboration
tutorial.step3Desc: Projects organize your conversations and resources.
tutorial.step3_1: Click the "+" button in the sidebar project list
tutorial.step3_2: Fill in the project name and description
tutorial.step3_3: You'll be taken into the project automatically
tutorial.step3_4: Click the settings icon (top-right) to open project settings
tutorial.step3Tip1: A project can bind multiple agents, knowledge bases, and MCP servers
tutorial.step4Desc: Bind agents, knowledge bases, and other resources to your project.
tutorial.step4_1: In project settings, switch to the "Agents" tab
tutorial.step4_2: Click "Bind Agent" and select the agents you created
tutorial.step4_3: Bind at least 2 agents to experience multi-agent collaboration
tutorial.step4_4: Switch to "General" tab and choose a collaboration mode (Parallel Coordinate / Parallel Aggregate)
tutorial.step4_5: Or switch to "Topology" tab to design a custom DAG topology (advanced)
tutorial.step4Tip1: For simple scenarios, use "Parallel Coordinate" — agents analyze in parallel, then a coordinator synthesizes
tutorial.step4Tip2: Advanced users can use the topology editor to design custom serial, parallel, and conditional workflows
tutorial.step5Desc: Upload documents to build a knowledge base for context-aware answers.
tutorial.step5_1: Go to "Knowledge Bases" in the sidebar
tutorial.step5_2: Create a knowledge base and configure chunking parameters
tutorial.step5_4: Bind the knowledge base in project settings
tutorial.step5Tip1: After uploading, wait for processing to complete (parse → chunk → vectorize). Status updates in real-time
tutorial.step6Desc: Connect MCP servers to give agents access to external tools.
tutorial.step6_1: Go to "MCP Servers" in the sidebar
tutorial.step6_2: Add an MCP server (supports SSE, HTTP, and Stdio protocols)
tutorial.step6_3: Click "Discover Tools" to fetch available tools
tutorial.step6_4: Bind the MCP server in project settings
tutorial.step7Desc: Use the visual editor to design custom multi-agent collaboration workflows.
tutorial.step7_1: In project settings, switch to the "Topology" tab
tutorial.step7_2: Drag nodes from the left panel onto the canvas (Agent, Coordinator, etc.)
tutorial.step7_3: Click a node to configure it in the right panel (select agent, set merge strategy, etc.)
tutorial.step7_4: Drag from a node's output port to another node's input port to create connections
tutorial.step7Tip1: Simplest topology: 2-3 Agent nodes → 1 Coordinator node
tutorial.step7Tip2: Coordinator deeply analyzes outputs; Aggregator simply merges; Passthrough forwards directly
tutorial.step7Warn1: The topology must be a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) — no circular connections allowed
tutorial.step8Desc: Monitor API calls, token consumption, and cost estimates.
tutorial.step8_2: View call records, statistics by provider/project
tutorial.step8_3: Filter by date range to see usage for specific periods
tutorial.startGuidedDesc: The system will guide you through each feature page with tips displayed at the top.
tutorial.bannerHint_step-1: Click "Add Provider", select a preset and enter your API Key. Then click "Mark as Done" to proceed.
tutorial.bannerHint_step-2: Click "Create Agent", fill in the name, system prompt, and select the LLM provider you just added. Create 2-3 agents with different roles.
tutorial.bannerHint_step-3: Click the "+" button in the sidebar to create a new project. Projects organize conversations and resources.
tutorial.bannerHint_step-4: In project settings, switch to the "Agents" tab and bind the agents you created. Bind at least 2 for multi-agent collaboration.
tutorial.bannerHint_step-5: Create a knowledge base and upload documents so agents can answer based on your data. You can skip this step.
tutorial.bannerHint_step-6: Add an MCP server to let agents call external tools. You can skip this step.
tutorial.bannerHint_step-7: In project settings under "Topology", drag nodes onto the canvas, connect and configure a custom collaboration workflow.
tutorial.bannerHint_step-8: Review API call counts, token consumption, and cost estimates on this page. The tutorial is complete after this step.
tutorial.topoNodeDesc_agent: The core node for AI reasoning. Each agent node is bound to a created agent, using its configured LLM model and system prompt for conversations.
tutorial.topoNodeExample_agent: e.g., "Tech Analyst" analyzes technical feasibility, "Market Researcher" analyzes market trends.
tutorial.topoNodeDesc_coordinator: Receives outputs from multiple upstream nodes and uses an LLM for deep synthesis. Analyzes biases, blind spots, and consensus points to produce high-quality conclusions.
tutorial.topoNodeExample_coordinator: Three analysts each provide their analysis; the coordinator produces a unified final report.
tutorial.topoNodeDesc_aggregator: Simply merges outputs from multiple upstream nodes. Unlike the coordinator, it doesn't perform deep analysis — just concatenates or briefly summarizes.
tutorial.topoNodeExample_aggregator: Collect information from multiple data sources and pass a simple summary downstream.
tutorial.topoNodeDesc_condition: Routes execution to different branches based on a condition expression. Uses an LLM to evaluate the condition and direct flow to the appropriate downstream node.
tutorial.topoNodeExample_condition: Route to "Technical" or "Business" agent based on the type of user question.
tutorial.topoNodeDesc_tool: Directly executes a specified MCP tool without LLM reasoning. Suitable for deterministic operations.
tutorial.topoNodeExample_tool: Call a database query tool to fetch real-time data, then pass it to a downstream agent for analysis.
tutorial.topoNodeDesc_rag: Retrieves relevant document fragments from specified knowledge bases. Results are passed as context to downstream nodes.
tutorial.topoNodeExample_rag: Retrieve product documentation to provide relevant context for an agent's response.
